踏板豎琴主要為藝術音樂設計，其調音踏板於1697年出現。1720年在巴伐利亞出現: The pedal harp is designed mainly for art music, and its tuning pedals appeared in 1697. A single-action mechanism appeared in Bavaria in 1720, able only to raise the pitch; double-action mechanisms were patented in London in 1801 and 1802, and the mechanism was doubled in 1807. This change let the pedals alter pitch, making it easy to play in any key, and so the harp entered the concerto and the opera house of the Baroque and Classical periods, and expanded through Romantic and twentieth-century classical music.
踏板豎琴主要用於藝術音樂，可獨奏、室內樂或管弦樂團；在浪漫時期與二十世紀古典音樂: The pedal harp is used mainly in art music, as a solo instrument, in chamber music or in the orchestra; in Romantic and twentieth-century classical music it matters because of the complexity of the harmony. It was a solo instrument in Baroque and Classical concertos and appeared in the opera houses of London, Paris and Berlin; Handel, Mozart, Boieldieu, Albrechtsberger, Schenk, Dussek and Spohr wrote concertos for it, and Mozart's Concerto for Flute and Harp is also mentioned. Berlioz, Liszt, the French and Russian Romantic composers and Puccini also used it in symphonic music and opera.
踏板豎琴屬弦鳴樂器，發聲靠手指撥弦與踏板改變音高。演奏時以拇指、食指、中指、無名: The pedal harp is a chordophone, sounding through the fingers plucking the strings and the pedals changing the pitch. The player touches the strings with the tips of thumb, index, middle and ring fingers, the little finger usually not being used because it is too short; the fingertips close towards the palm so that the string leaves the pressure and vibrates. Seven pedals each control all the strings of one note name, and their three positions, up, middle and down, put the strings a semitone flat, natural or a semitone sharp; with nothing operated the instrument is tuned throughout to C flat major. A beginner should concentrate on finger position, control of force and setting the pedals; different plucking points give a full sound or a nasal one, and studies are used to build fingering and control.

The body consists of an upright pillar, a soundboard, a curved neck and a base with seven pedals, and the source does not state the wood or metal materials of these parts. The sounding body is the strings, usually forty-seven; the lowest are of copper or steel wound with nylon, the lower middle strings are gut, the middle to upper strings nylon, and all or more of them may be gut. The total tension of the strings on the soundboard is about one tonne. The source does not describe the materials of the other mechanical parts such as the links, cables, discs and pins.
踏板豎琴為弦鳴樂器，常見於非洲、歐洲、亞洲、美洲，以踏板改變弦長，可奏各調。通常: The pedal harp is a chordophone, common in Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas, whose pedals change the length of the strings so that it can play in any key. It usually has 47 strings, seven to the octave, a range of about six and a half octaves from C♭1 to G♭7. Volume is controlled by the force of the fingertip pluck; the plucking point affects the timbre, the middle of the string being fuller and the bottom end nasal, close to a guitar. Compared with folk, plectrum or Celtic harps, the pedal mechanism can change pitch in both directions; unlike the fully chromatic double-strung, triple-strung (Welsh) and cross-strung harps, it still has only seven strings to the octave.

The pedal harp (also called the concert harp) is a large, technically modern chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 322.222, designed mainly for art music. Its construction includes an upright pillar, a soundboard, a curved neck containing the mechanism, and seven pedals at the base; it usually has 47 strings, seven to the octave, with a range of about six and a half octaves. The player plucks with the tips of thumb, index, middle and ring fingers, the little finger generally not being used. The pedals change the pitch so that the instrument can play in any key. It can be played solo, or used in chamber ensembles or in the orchestra.
